nodes.title: Build a Vite-native component workbench with a small deep core and explicit framework adapters
Let a user run the workbench against an unmodified Vite 8 config
Delegating the hard parts to Vite 8 (Rolldown, Oxc, Environment API) beats wrapping it
Thinness is measured by the Vite contact surface, not by LoC or feature count
Ladle watermark

detail.definition: The invariant bundle of Ladle behaviors the successor must preserve: canonical story identity, metadata coherence, URL-backed shell state, lazy story loading, preview/full-shell mode, provider/decorator/args semantics, metadata export, and optional capability gating.

nodes.title: Vite contact surface

detail.definition: The enumerable set of Vite APIs, plugin hooks, config keys, and conventions the workbench depends on. The measurable dimension of 'thin'; tracked as a reviewable artifact in docs/vite-contact-surface.md.

nodes.title: Normalized story graph

detail.definition: The canonical internal model of stories, identities, hierarchy, provenance, metadata, and lazy runtime handles, authoritative across dev runtime, build outputs, and metadata export.

nodes.title: Shell state

detail.definition: URL-backed workbench UI state such as selected story, mode, theme, source visibility, width, and controls.

nodes.title: Capability plugin

detail.definition: An optional shell feature layered over the story graph and shell state; disabled capabilities impose no bundle, startup, or conceptual cost.

nodes.title: False-thinness

detail.definition: The anti-pattern of calling a tool a 'thin wrapper' while smuggling a full SPA, runtime, and shell through a plugin API. Thinness applies to the Vite contact surface, not to the workbench's own product scope.

nodes.title: No-React invariant

detail.definition: The workbench depends on zero React packages; React is resolved at runtime from the user's node_modules, and static import of react/react-dom from product source is forbidden by ESLint and proven by a seed-check.

nodes.title: Vite 8 just shipped and Ladle does not integrate well with it
The Vite framework-plugin ecosystem standardized on a thin-adapter-over-Vite pattern
Ladle is treated as the characterization corpus and current-state recovery (companion liftout)
Workbench consumes user Vite config via Vite's own resolution primitives, with no hand-rolled merge
Architecture is explicitly split into core, Vite host binding, and framework adapter responsibilities
Story discovery produces stable canonical IDs, hierarchical navigation data, provenance, and metadata
The shell is URL-backed and can reproduce selected story and shell state from the URL
Provide a machine-readable manifest/metadata surface coherent with runtime story identity
Optional capabilities can be enabled or disabled without becoming mandatory core cost
Story transitions must not leak story-scoped controls or other transient story-local state
Controls defaults come from the manifest, not from mod.args on the dynamically-imported story module
Controls defaults are read client-side from the dynamically-imported story module's args export
Vite 8's Rolldown, Oxc, and Environment API are sufficient to make a genuinely thin workbench possible
Vite's single-environment composition primitives suffice to layer over arbitrary user configs (validated)
Dev catalog reads can be memoized without making story metadata stale (validated)
A normalized story graph can stay framework-agnostic even when authoring syntax is adapter-specific
The workbench supports Vite 8.x only; Vite 5/6/7 are never supported
No hand-rolled Vite config merging; insufficient primitives are filed upstream, not worked around
The workbench depends on zero React packages, enforced at the import site
Preserve the user's Vite root; do not relocate root into node_modules the way Ladle does
core/ must not import host, adapter, or cli (Shape D internal boundary)
Only the host mutates URL state; capabilities propose changes but cannot apply them
Disabled capabilities are unreachable even by manual import
Adopt Shape D: single package with lint-enforced internal module split

detail.chosen_option: One package (packages/fable/) with internal core/host/adapter/capabilities/cli directories whose import boundaries are ESLint-enforced
rejected: Shape B monorepo of separate packages up front
Flat single module with no enforced boundaries
detail.rationale: Single publish and one package.json keep shipping simple while lint boundaries keep the import graph already-correct for a future monorepo split.

nodes.title: Compose user config through Vite's own primitives, not a merge layer

detail.chosen_option: loadConfigFromFile to obtain the user config, spread into inline config passed to createServer with configFile:false, append workbench plugins, preserve user root
rejected: Hand-rolled merge of user config and workbench config into a third object
Relocating root into node_modules like Ladle
detail.rationale: Vite's resolver and plugin-composition rules keep the contact surface small and the workbench robust to Vite updates.

nodes.title: Use a window-event protocol as the single host-capability seam

detail.chosen_option: fable:story-change and fable:shell-mode-change (host to capability) plus fable:navigate-args (capability to host), with strict listen/dispatch asymmetry
rejected: A shared shell-state module graph crossing the capability boundary
Direct capability mutation of URL state
detail.rationale: Events are a single typed seam that keeps capabilities decoupled while only the host applies state changes.

nodes.title: Map virtual ids to real on-disk files for static browser product code

detail.chosen_option: Static browser modules (browser-entry, url-codec, each capability runtime) live as real .ts files whose virtual:fable/<id> resolves to the file path so Vite's TS transform runs
rejected: Keep all browser code on the \0virtual: escape hatch
detail.rationale: Real files get type-checking and the default TS transform; only computed modules and the no-React adapter runtime stay string-template generators, a principled asymmetry.
